items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: So the next job Roy gave me was playing with Tick Chambers, Richard Jones, and myself...

ctx.x: S-T-O-R-O-D-E. Conant? Yeah, Trum. He was good too. Yeah, a lot of fellows used to have him. You never heard of Nene Bryant even had him. He was a drummer, a good one. He played with Tick Chambers at Miss Cole Lawnbottom. And there was a kid around there, he died young, Jim Williams. And he used to, we couldn't go in the pool room, but he had long parents on, he had long parents. He was considered a man. And he sat on the pool room table and played for us. Now later on they said he was going to be one of the…
And he wrote a lot of tunes too, you know.

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: That's where I'd hear them. And so there was Tick Chambers... Tick was playing there, you see?

ctx.x: That's where I'd hear them. And so there was Tick Chambers, Kohl's, Lawn Parties on Josephine Street. Tick was playing there, you see? So I mean it just was one of those things where you had to hear that music. And on every Monday or Sunday there was advertisement, here comes a horse and wagon, I guess that's where that tailgate come, because the trombone player was always on the end, because he needed room for his slide. So that's why I said I'm very fortunate to have been born in New Orleans and I'm grateful…
How do you spell that name, the Careers, do you remember?
